exercise.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Snatch

reference.title: Dumbbell One Arm Snatch
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Weightlifting, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (first pull from the floor, explosive triple extension, high pull, overhead catch on one arm)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the floor, hold through the pull and the catch, breathe out standing with the arm locked.
breathing.cadence: Smooth first pull, about 0.5 s from the hang to the catch

prescription.tempo: Controlled first pull, explosive second pull, stick the lockout
prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell light enough to move fast (a lighter one than for the clean); stop while every rep stays crisp. Lake 2006 tested 80-100% of the dumbbell snatch 1RM in trained weightlifters.
prescription.frequency: 1-2 times a week, early in the session
prescription.progression: Hang snatch first; add load while the lockout stays solid, alternate arms

cues.text: Feet a little wider than the hips, dumbbell between the feet, hips back, flat back, free arm relaxed.
Push the floor away, knees out, chest up.
Jump through the floor, shrug, pull the elbow high with the dumbbell close.
Punch up and under: catch on a straight arm in a quarter squat.
Stand tall with the arm locked, biceps by the ear.
Hold: dumbbell over the shoulder, ribs down.
Lower to the shoulder, to the hip, then hinge it back to the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing the dumbbell out at the top
mistakes.fix: Drop under it and punch: the arm locks as the legs catch.

mistakes.mistake: Dumbbell swinging away from the body
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow high and the dumbbell close.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the floor
mistakes.fix: Hips back, chest up; start from the hang if needed.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting or bending sideways under the weight
mistakes.fix: Brace and keep the shoulders square.

kinematics.norm: Hips below the shoulders, back flat, load between the feet (clinical opinion, after NSCA Essentials for the barbell start)
Quarter squat with the arm locked overhead (clinical opinion); the dumbbell snatch loads the two sides unevenly through the pull and the catch (Lake 2006)
Controlled first pull, explosive second pull (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #388812, Dumbbell One Arm Snatch, video (movement reference)
Lake, Lauder & Dyson 2006, kinetic analysis of a unilateral snatch movement (ISBS 2006 conference proceedings)
Lauder & Lake 2008, biomechanical comparison of unilateral and bilateral power snatch lifts (J Strength Cond Res 22(3):653-660)
McGill & Marshall 2012, kettlebell swing, snatch, and bottoms-up carry: back and hip muscle activation, motion, and low back loads (J Strength Cond Res 26(1):16-27)

Caulfield, Hornsby & Haff, power exercises: power clean (and hang power clean variation), excerpt from NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 5th edition (Haff & Triplett, eds.; Human Kinetics)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Fast lifts: learn the positions slowly with a light dumbbell first, keep the dumbbells close to the body and clear a space around you.
Shoulder pain overhead: skip the snatch or stop at the high pull.
If the lockout fails, step away and let the dumbbell come down beside you.
modify: Low-back pain or limited hip mobility: start from the hang (dumbbell at the knees).
progressions: Barbell power snatch with coaching (Lauder 2008 compared the two).

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drive the explosive hip extension; the snatch reached about 58% MVC in the gluteus maximus in a kettlebell snatch (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drive the explosive hip extension; the snatch reached about 58% MVC in the gluteus maximus in a kettlebell snatch (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Push the floor away and absorb the quarter-squat catch.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Push the floor away and absorb the quarter-squat catch.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Load the hinge off the floor and extend the hips.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Load the hinge off the floor and extend the hips.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Rise onto the balls of the feet at the top of the drive.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Rise onto the balls of the feet at the top of the drive.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Shrug the working shoulder, then hold the shoulder blade up under the lockout.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lift the elbow high and out.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Punch the dumbbell up as you drop under it.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hips from the wide start.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hips from the wide start.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk bending and twisting toward the weight; in dumbbell snatches the force on the two feet differed between sides (Lake 2006).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk bending and twisting toward the weight; in dumbbell snatches the force on the two feet differed between sides (Lake 2006).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a flat back from the floor (about 54% MVC lower erector activity in the kettlebell snatch, McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a flat back from the floor (about 54% MVC lower erector activity in the kettlebell snatch, McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blade up for the lockout.

guides.label: Close to the body, punch under
